title: NDMA National Guidelines: Heatwave Safety - Do's During Extreme Heat
source: IMD-NDMA National Heatwave Safety Guidelines
text:
## Do's During Extreme Heat (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 1)
- Listen to Radio, watch TV, read newspaper for local weather news or download weather information mobile apps.
- Drink sufficient water and stay hydrated even if not thirsty. Persons on fluid-restricted diets should consult a doctor before increasing intake.
- Use ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution), homemade drinks like lassi, torani (rice water), lemon water, buttermilk, and coconut water to keep yourself hydrated.
- Wear lightweight, light-coloured, loose, and porous cotton clothes.
- If outside, cover your head: use a cloth, hat, or umbrella. Use sunglasses to protect eyes and sunscreen to protect skin.
- Provide resting shade, clean drinking water, buttermilk, first-aid kits with ice-packs and ORS for all workers at workplaces.
- Schedule strenuous jobs to cooler times of the day; increase frequency and length of rest breaks for outdoor activities.
- In case of heat stroke emergencies, call National Emergency helpline 112 or Disaster helpline 1077.

title: NDMA National Guidelines: Heatwave Safety - Don'ts During Extreme Heat
source: IMD-NDMA National Heatwave Safety Guidelines
text:
## Don'ts During Extreme Heat (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 3)
- Avoid going out in direct sun, especially between 12:00 noon and 3:00 PM.
- Avoid strenuous outdoor activities when outside during peak afternoon hours.
- Do not leave children or pets alone inside parked locked vehicles under direct sunlight.
- Avoid cooking during peak hours; open doors and windows to ventilate cooking area adequately.
- Avoid alcohol, tea, coffee, and carbonated soft drinks, which dehydrate the body.
- Avoid high-protein, salty, spicy, and oily food. Do not eat stale food.
- Avoid using incandescent light bulbs and appliances which generate unnecessary heat.

title: NDMA National Guidelines: Heatwave Safety - Treatment of Sunstroke and Vulnerable Groups
source: IMD-NDMA National Heatwave Safety Guidelines
text:
## Treatment of Sunstroke and Vulnerable Groups (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 2-3)
- Special care for vulnerable groups: infants, young children, pregnant women, the elderly, sick or overweight individuals are more likely to become victims of excessive heat.
- Cool indoor spaces with curtains, fans, damp clothing, and frequent cold water baths; keep windows closed during day and open at night.
- Treatment of a person affected by sunstroke: use a wet cloth or pour cool water on the victim's head and neck.
- Give the affected person ORS, lemon water, or torani to drink to rehydrate the body.
- If experiencing persistently high body temperature, throbbing headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, or disorientation, seek medical attention immediately.
- Call National Emergency helpline 112 or Disaster Management helpline 1077 for urgent medical assistance.

title: NDMA National Guidelines: Cold Wave Safety - Do's During Cold Wave
source: IMD-NDMA National Cold Wave Safety Guidelines
text:
## Do's During Cold Wave (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 1)
- Have adequate winter clothing. Multiple layers of loose-fitting, lightweight clothing are more effective than one thick layer.
- Have emergency supplies, warm blankets, and medical necessities ready.
- Stay indoors as much as possible; minimise travel to prevent exposure to severe cold wind.
- Keep dry; if clothes get wet, change quickly to prevent loss of body heat.
- Prefer mittens over gloves; mittens provide better warmth and insulation from cold.
- Keep head, neck, hands, and feet warmly covered with caps, mufflers, gloves, and socks.
- Drink hot drinks regularly to maintain body temperature.
- Ensure adequate ventilation and fresh airflow when using charcoal angithi, coal braziers, or kerosene heaters indoors to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

title: NDMA National Guidelines: Cold Wave Safety - Don'ts, Hypothermia and Frostbite Treatment
source: IMD-NDMA National Cold Wave Safety Guidelines
text:
## Don'ts, Hypothermia and Frostbite Treatment (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 1-2)
- Do not drink alcohol in extreme cold; alcohol dilates blood vessels and reduces core body temperature.
- Do not ignore shivering; shivering is the first warning sign that the body is losing heat and a signal to return indoors.
- Watch out for symptoms of frostbite: numbness, white or pale appearance on fingers, toes, ear lobes, and tip of the nose.
- Put areas affected by frostbite in warm (not hot) water; do not massage or rub frostbitten areas vigorously, as this causes tissue damage.
- Hypothermia first aid: move person to a warm room, change wet clothes, rewarm body with dry blankets and warm drinks (never alcohol).
- Seek medical attention immediately if body temperature drops or disorientation occurs.

title: NDMA National Guidelines: Cold Wave Safety - Vulnerable Groups and Winter Shelter
source: IMD-NDMA National Cold Wave Safety Guidelines
text:
## Vulnerable Groups and Winter Shelter (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 1 & 3)
- Special protection for vulnerable populations: newborn infants, elderly individuals, chronically ill persons, and homeless citizens.
- Maintain comfortable indoor room temperature and protect children and elderly from drafts.
- District administrations provide night shelters (Rain Baseras) equipped with blankets and hot water for homeless persons during severe cold wave.
- Emergency assistance and shelter helplines: call National Emergency helpline 112 or Disaster helpline 1077.
- Domestic cattle and pets protection: keep animals inside sheds at night, provide dry bedding, protect from cold winds, and increase protein/mineral rations.

title: Heat Action Plan Framework - Early Warning System and Temperature Thresholds
source: Delhi Disaster Management Authority State Heat Action Plan
text:
## Early Warning System and Temperature Thresholds (Source: DDMA Heat Action Plan, Page 10 & 42)
- District administrations and municipal corporations activate Heat Action Plans based on forecasted temperature thresholds.
- Alert levels: Yellow Watch (Hot day advisory >= 40 °C in plains), Orange Alert (Be Prepared for severe heat stress), and Red Warning (Take Action for extreme heat conditions).
- Inter-agency coordination: Nodal disaster officers coordinate municipal water tankers, public drinking water kiosks (Piyau), and emergency health centres.
- Public awareness campaigns and early warnings disseminated via SMS, mobile apps, local media, and transit announcements 24 to 48 hours in advance.

title: Heat Action Plan Framework - Outdoor Labour Protection and Working Hours
source: Delhi Disaster Management Authority State Heat Action Plan
text:
## Outdoor Labour Protection and Working Hours (Source: DDMA Heat Action Plan, Page 69 & 81)
- Labour Department mandates rescheduling working hours for outdoor construction labourers and agricultural workers.
- Shift working hours to cooler morning hours (6:00 AM to 11:00 AM) and late afternoon (after 4:00 PM).
- Mandatory afternoon work stoppage between 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM during declared Orange and Red alert days.
- Employers must provide on-site shaded resting areas, clean drinking water, ORS hydration packets, and first-aid facilities.
- Mobile medical vans deployed at high-density labour hotspots to provide emergency medical support.

title: Heat Action Plan Framework - Cool Roof Systems and Passive Urban Cooling
source: Delhi Disaster Management Authority State Heat Action Plan
text:
## Cool Roof Systems and Passive Urban Cooling (Source: DDMA Heat Action Plan, Page 88-89)
- Cool roofs utilize high-albedo (reflective) materials and solar-reflective white paint to reduce surface temperatures.
- Application of cool roof coatings lowers indoor temperatures by 2 °C to 5 °C, improving indoor thermal comfort.
- Cool roofs achieve significant energy savings by reducing air-conditioning and fan power requirements.
- Reduces urban heat island effect across densely populated settlements and low-income slum households.
- Incorporates cross-ventilation, shading sunshades, green vegetative roofs, and reflective exterior building coatings.

title: Official Weather Warning Colour-Code Definitions - Green: No Warning (Normal)
source: IMD Weather Warning Colour Code System
text:
## Green: No Warning (Normal Weather)
- Official Label: Green – No Warning.
- Meaning: Atmospheric and weather conditions are normal, comfortable, and safe. No severe or hazardous weather expected.
- Action Required: No advisory or emergency action is required. Citizens, transport networks, and commercial operations continue day-to-day activities normally without disruption.

title: Official Weather Warning Colour-Code Definitions - Yellow: Watch (Be Updated)
source: IMD Weather Warning Colour Code System
text:
## Yellow: Watch (Be Updated)
- Official Label: Yellow – Watch.
- Meaning: Severely bad weather or adverse conditions are possible over the next few days. The situation is developing and carries uncertainty.
- Action Required: Be updated / Be aware. Citizens, travelers, and disaster response teams should keep track of the latest weather forecasts, nowcasts, and official bulletins as conditions may worsen.

title: Official Weather Warning Colour-Code Definitions - Orange: Alert (Be Prepared)
source: IMD Weather Warning Colour Code System
text:
## Orange: Alert (Be Prepared)
- Official Label: Orange – Alert.
- Meaning: Weather conditions have deteriorated and have the potential to cause significant disruptions, transport delays, power outages, and threat to life and property.
- Action Required: Be prepared / Alert. Authorities must prepare contingency plans, preposition rescue teams, and inspect drainage/power networks. Citizens should keep emergency supplies, medicines, water, and backup lights ready.

title: Official Weather Warning Colour-Code Definitions - Red: Warning (Take Action)
source: IMD Weather Warning Colour Code System
text:
## Red: Warning (Take Action)
- Official Label: Red – Warning (Take Action).
- Meaning: Extremely severe weather conditions are imminent or ongoing with high impact, extreme risk to life, and catastrophic damage to infrastructure.
- Action Required: Take action immediately. Emergency response authorities (NDMA, SDMA, District Administration) deploy NDRF/SDRF teams and execute mandatory evacuation from low-lying or vulnerable areas. Citizens must stay in safe shelters and avoid all travel.

title: Flood, Cyclone and Lightning Safety Guidelines - Flood Do's and Don'ts
source: IMD-NDMA National Floods Safety Guidelines
text:
## Flood Do's and Don'ts (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 1-2)
- Before and during floods: ignore rumours, stay calm, and don't panic.
- Keep mobile phones charged for emergency communication.
- Turn off gas valves and electrical power mains before flood water enters premises.
- Do not drive into flooded roads; as little as 30 cm (1 foot) of moving water can float a car.
- Stay away from flooded streets, drainage channels, culverts, and downed electrical poles or hanging power lines.
- Evacuate immediately to designated high ground or cyclone/flood shelters when advised by district administration.
- Do not allow children to play in or near flood waters; water may be contaminated and carry disease.

title: Flood, Cyclone and Lightning Safety Guidelines - Cyclone and Lightning Safety Measures
source: IMD-NDMA Cyclone and Thunderstorm Guidelines
text:
## Cyclone and Lightning Safety Measures (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 1-3)
- Cyclone precautions: inspect and secure loose roof tiles or tin sheets; board or tape glass windows.
- Keep emergency kits ready: non-perishable food, potable drinking water, torches, battery radio, and first-aid supplies.
- Unhook and disconnect electrical appliances during cyclones to prevent short-circuits and electrical fires.
- Lightning safety 30/30 rule: if the time between lightning flash and thunder is less than 30 seconds, take shelter indoors; wait 30 minutes after last thunder before heading outdoors.
- If outdoor during lightning: avoid tall isolated trees, open fields, elevated ridges, and metal structures; if hair stands on neck, squat low with hands on knees.

title: ICAR Agricultural Weather Advisory - Extreme Heat and Drought Crop Management
source: IMD Agrimet National Agricultural Guidance
text:
## Extreme Heat and Drought Crop Management (Source: IMD Agrimet Agriculture Guidance, Page 4)
- Apply light and frequent irrigation to standing crops during evening or early morning hours to maintain root zone moisture and reduce soil surface temperature.
- Increase frequency of irrigation during critical crop growth stages (tillering, flowering, grain filling).
- Mulch with crop residue, straw, or polythene sheets to conserve soil moisture and suppress evaporative loss.
- Use sprinkler and drip irrigation systems to optimize water use efficiency under heat stress.
- Protect farm animals and cattle: keep animals under shade, provide ample cool drinking water, cool sheds with straw/dung-mud plaster or water foggers, and graze only during cooler morning and evening hours.

title: ICAR Agricultural Weather Advisory - Cold Wave, Frost and Ground Freeze Crop Protection
source: IMD Agrimet National Agricultural Guidance
text:
## Cold Wave, Frost and Ground Freeze Crop Protection (Source: IMD Agrimet Agriculture Guidance, Page 2-3)
- Apply light and frequent irrigation or sprinkler irrigation in evening hours to protect crops from cold injury and ground frost.
- In rice nursery beds: cover nursery beds with polythene sheets during the night and remove in the morning; irrigate in the evening and drain out in the morning.
- Cover young orchard fruit plants with straw, sarkanda, gunny bags, or polythene sheets.
- To protect sensitive crops like mustard, gram, and rajmah from frost injury, spray dilute sulphuric acid @ 0.1% (1 L in 1000 L water) or thiourea @ 500 ppm.
- Animal husbandry in winter: keep cattle and goats inside sheds during night, provide dry bedding, and supplement daily feed with mineral mixtures, salt, and jaggery.

title: ICAR Agricultural Weather Advisory - Flood, Waterlogging and Standing Crop Protection
source: IMD Agrimet National Agricultural Guidance
text:
## Flood, Waterlogging and Standing Crop Protection (Source: IMD Agrimet Floods Guidance, Page 3)
- Provide adequate field drainage channels to immediately drain excess stagnant water from submerged crop fields.
- Stake and provide mechanical support to tall crops like banana, sugarcane, and vegetables to prevent lodging from heavy rain and squally winds.
- Postpone spraying of chemical pesticides and application of fertilizers during periods of heavy rainfall and high soil moisture.
- Once flood water recedes, apply top dressing with nitrogen fertilizer or foliar spray of 1% to 2% urea / potassium nitrate solution to promote rapid crop root recovery and rejuvenate standing plants.

title: Coastal and Fisherfolk Marine Weather Safety Guidance - Sea Venture Restrictions and Weather Warnings
source: IMD Marine Cyclone & Fishermen Warning Bulletin
text:
## Sea Venture Restrictions and Weather Warnings (Source: IMD Marine Fishermen Warning Bulletin, Page 1)
- Fishermen are strictly advised not to venture into the sea when squally weather with wind speed reaching 45-55 kmph gusting to 65 kmph is expected.
- Sea conditions during squally weather and cyclonic storms are rough to very rough over coastal and offshore sea areas.
- Fisherfolk already out at sea must return immediately to the nearest coast, harbor, or designated safe anchorage.
- Deep-sea fishing vessels must strictly avoid venturing into central and deep sea regions during active gale and storm warnings (wind speeds 65-85 kmph gusting to 95 kmph).

title: Coastal and Fisherfolk Marine Weather Safety Guidance - Squally Weather and Deep Sea Safety Measures
source: IMD Marine Cyclone & Fishermen Warning Bulletin
text:
## Squally Weather and Deep Sea Safety Measures (Source: IMD Marine Fishermen Warning Bulletin, Page 1)
- All fishing vessels and motorized boats must carry operational marine communication gear: VHF/SSB radios, GPS navigators, and NAVTEX receivers.
- Maintain real-time contact with coastal fisheries stations and Coast Guard emergency frequencies.
- Every person on board must wear certified life jackets; inspect life-saving appliances, buoyant distress signals, and distress beacons (EPIRBs) before sailing.
- Anchor boats securely at coastal jetties, bays, or haul craft onto high ground above the maximum spring tide level during storm surge and cyclone alerts.
